correctness.rationale: Exact rational-power-sum representation, coefficientwise Euler shift identity, and p-integral specialization prove the congruence for all n,p,k. The first failure of any potential period is equivalent to first failure of the known P period, by propagation along another period. Ternary F_n ≡ 2^n−1 (mod 3) gives the complete parity-based onset; independent modular recurrence and rational computation agree in 17 test grids. Finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The known Carmichael period and onset bound in arXiv:2409.03799 do not imply the new exact defect, necessary-and-sufficient onset criterion, or alternating ternary onset. residual_risks: Older specialized notes (including the original 1962 last-digit work) were not inspected at full length. An equivalent scalar preperiod formula could be present there.

value.rationale: The least start of eventual periodicity is a natural arithmetic invariant; published results determine the period and upper-bound its onset but do not determine the exact index where the periodic tail begins. The universal prime-power shift defect gives a local arithmetic obstruction and a finite exact algorithm, while the ternary case has a complete nonconstant infinite classification, revealing infinitely many genuine cancellations at odd exponents.
